solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Who needs to discharge jet?

parts.note: the person who must discharge a jet of water is the one tackling a blaze; 'discharge' teases a gun being fired

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about who has to empty a jet, perhaps an aircraft or a fountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The jet is of water from a hose, and the discharging is part of putting out a blaze, not firing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sprays jets of water from a hose is an emergency service crew member tackling blazes.

clue.text: One who's turned out well following a little work

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
OP, short for opus, is a work, and the abbreviation is a little one

explanation.surface: Someone who has done well after only a small piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out well' means dressed smartly, not succeeded.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a man excessively concerned with dressing smartly, someone always well turned out.

clue.text: Work in charge of collection of old letters

parts.note: to run is to work or operate, as a machine runs

explanation.surface: A job running a collection of historic correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: The old letters are alphabet characters, runes, not correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes are the characters of ancient Germanic alphabets, so the adjective describes those old letters.

clue.text: Obese throughout the year, so as to cause death

parts.note: obese means fat
all, as in all year, means throughout
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A warning that being overweight all year round can kill you.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes something done in a deadly manner, with lethal effect.

clue.text: Turkish town girl tops sauce with unusual oil

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the next one

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
sauce and lip both mean cheek or impudence

indicators.note: unusual signals that the word oil is rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: A girl pours sauce over a dish, then adds some odd oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' is impudence, not a condiment. 'unusual' makes OLI from OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli is a town on the Dardanelles in Turkey, scene of the 1915 campaign.

clue.text: Steak is black in colour

indicators.note: in places the black inside the word for colour

parts.note: a tone is a shade or colour
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Remarks on a piece of beef being black.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef containing a T-shaped bone from the loin.

clue.text: Wild orpin conceals a minute bellflower

indicators.note: conceals means the rearranged plant word holds the next pieces inside it
wild tells us the letters of orpin run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild sedum plant hides a tiny bellflower among its leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' turns ORPIN into RPION, and 'conceals' tucks AM inside it after the R. Orpine is itself a plant, which makes the surface botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampion is a European campanula, a member of the bellflower family grown for its edible root.

clue.text: Miss all but the last runner

indicators.note: all but the last says the final letter is dropped from the word for miss

parts.note: to skip something is to miss it out

explanation.surface: Failing to catch every runner except the final one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is a ski running over snow, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long narrow runner fixed to a boot for gliding over snow, like a sledge's runner.

clue.text: Flirty woman succeeded without clothing size for the smaller figure?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
ex is Latin for out of, without, as in ex dividend
kit is a set of clothing, as in football kit
ten is a small dress size in the UK, worn by a slim woman

explanation.surface: A flirt managed without clothes, which suits a slim figure.
explanation.walkthrough: UK dress sizes run in even numbers; size 10 is for a slim figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A sex kitten is a young woman who plays up her flirtatious sexual appeal.

clue.text: Puzzling G in preamble is beyond doubt

indicators.note: puzzling suggests the letters of the phrase are confused and need sorting into a new order

explanation.surface: A solver baffled by a stray letter G in a puzzle's preamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unassailable, which no argument can overturn, is beyond doubt.

clue.text: Fine distinction made by peacekeepers in politic manoeuvring

indicators.note: in puts the peacekeepers inside the rearranged letters
manoeuvring tells us the letters of politic are moved about

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the familiar United Nations forces

explanation.surface: A subtle point made by peacekeeping forces in diplomatic manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' makes PCTILIO; 'in' slots the peacekeepers' two letters after its opening P. 'Politic' reads as an adjective but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctilio is a fine point of etiquette or a nice distinction in conduct.

clue.text: I vote for everyone to stop politician's confusion

indicators.note: to stop means the pieces plug the gap between the politician's two letters

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
an X is the cross marked on a ballot paper to vote
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Someone casting a vote for all, to block a politician's confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: U is a British film rating meaning suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A mix-up is a muddle or a confused mistake.

clue.text: Sick in one taxi on the way back — are these to blame?

indicators.note: in puts the sick word inside the reversed pair
on the way back says the one-and-taxi pair is read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a cab is a taxi
sick means ill

explanation.surface: Someone falling ill in a taxi going home wonders what caused it.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed pair gives BACI, and ILL goes in before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are the likely culprits when someone falls ill, so they could be blamed for sickness.

clue.text: Papers are gripped by this person in university office going on strike

indicators.note: going on means the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: a bulldog is a proctor's attendant at Oxford or Cambridge universities
to clip is to hit or strike

explanation.surface: A university official's paperwork is held by someone going on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge, bulldogs are officers who help the proctors keep discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong sprung clip holds a sheaf of documents together.

clue.text: Building only half used, despite being cool

indicators.note: only half means just the second half of the word used is kept

parts.note: if can mean even though or despite, as in 'pleasant if dull'
to ice something is to cool it

explanation.surface: A building half empty, even though it's a cool place.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large imposing structure.

clue.text: Put up with yogurt initially like cottage cheese?

parts.note: to lump it is to put up with something unwelcome

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of yogurt

explanation.surface: Tolerating yogurt, at first, as being like cottage cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottage cheese has a curdy texture full of small clots, an example of something with bits in it.

clue.text: Make of car to experiment with inlaid work

parts.note: a marque is a brand or make of car
to try is to experiment

explanation.surface: A car manufacturer experiments with inlaid decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Marquetry is decorative veneer of wood pieces set into furniture surfaces.

clue.text: Playwright about to ring character in Chicken Run?

indicators.note: about means the playwright's name goes round the ring

parts.note: Joe Orton was an English playwright, author of Loot
a ping is a ringing sound

explanation.surface: A dramatist set to phone someone about a role in the animated film Chicken Run.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicken Run is a film about hens, so its characters are poultry breeds of a sort.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orpington is a breed of domestic hen, so it fits a cast of chickens.

clue.text: Simple plant toxin trapping a noble Roman

parts.note: pat can mean glib or simple, as in a pat answer

indicators.note: trapping means the toxin word encloses the next letter

parts.note: ricin is a poison from castor oil plant seeds

explanation.surface: A basic toxin from a plant ensnares an aristocrat of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Patricians were the hereditary aristocracy of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Evolutionary pioneer's success is seen in small river fish

indicators.note: seen in says these pieces sit inside the fish

parts.note: dart is an old name for the dace, a small river fish
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A naturalist's triumph is spotted among small fish in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'the evolutionary pioneer's man', a follower of the theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Charles Darwin's theory of evolution belongs to that pioneer.

clue.text: Siberian diamonds need cutting

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
a cutting wind is a bitterly cold one

explanation.surface: Diamonds from Siberia must be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siberian' is an adjective for freezing weather, not a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is a byword for freezing weather, so a Siberian wind is a frigid one.

clue.text: Study origins of extraordinarily blue star

parts.note: a den is a private room or study

indicators.note: origins of means the starting letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Studying where an unusually blue star comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Deneb is the brightest star in the constellation Cygnus.

clue.text: Free spirit? Fall unconscious!

parts.note: a drop is a fall
out cold means unconscious

explanation.surface: A cheerful soul suddenly collapses senseless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rejects conventional society and lives unconstrained is a kind of free spirit.

clue.text: Meals cut down all round after overabundance of big muscles

indicators.note: after places the trimmed meals behind the overabundance

parts.note: a glut is an overabundance

indicators.note: cut down all round means the word meals loses its letters at both ends

explanation.surface: Smaller meals all round after overeating builds big muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: The gluteal muscles of the buttocks are the body's largest, so the adjective relates to big muscles.

clue.text: Substitute copper for one ring in weaving machine

indicators.note: for signals that copper replaces one of the ring letters

parts.note: a loom weaves cloth
O is shaped like a ring
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Swapping a copper part for a ring in a loom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute' looks like the instruction but is the definition; 'for' does the swapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or priest standing in for another, a temporary replacement.

clue.text: Anger about working silver when another metal was being worked

definitions.text: when another metal was being worked

indicators.note: about means the anger word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: ire is anger
on means working, as a machine is on
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Fury over silversmithing when some other metal was in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The era after the Bronze Age when iron tools came into use.

clue.text: A cat and a dog from Japan

parts.note: a kit is a young cat, a kitten

explanation.surface: A cat and a dog, both from Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Akita is a large spitz breed originally from Japan.

clue.text: Good deal closed game

parts.note: a lot is a good deal, a large amount
a door pushed to is closed

explanation.surface: A good bargain struck, a deal closed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance like bingo or a lottery.

clue.text: Early part of costume fabricated liner keeping in hoop shape?

definitions.text: Early part of costume fabricated liner keeping in hoop shape?

indicators.note: early part of says take the first letter of costume
keeping means the rearranged letters hold the next pieces
fabricated signals the letters of liner are made up into a new order

parts.note: O is shaped like a hoop

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's lining keeps a skirt in a hooped shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabricated' makes RLINE, and 'keeping' holds the next two pieces just after its R. The whole clue also describes the garment itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A crinoline is a stiff hooped petticoat holding out a Victorian skirt, a lining that kept a hoop shape.

clue.text: Ruminant of arable wetlands

indicators.note: of signals the letters come from within the words arable wetlands

explanation.surface: A cud-chewing animal from farmland and marshes.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is a cud-chewing animal.

clue.text: Work steadily at college to avoid getting second

indicators.note: to avoid getting second means the second letter of the college word is dropped

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a kind of college

explanation.surface: A student works hard at college to avoid getting a second-class degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is the second letter, not a degree class. A poly was a British polytechnic college.
explanation.definitionFit: To ply a trade is to work at it steadily and diligently.

clue.text: Prove modern taste is degenerate

indicators.note: is degenerate signals the letters of modern taste decay into a new order

explanation.surface: An argument that contemporary taste has decayed.
explanation.definitionFit: To prove something is to show it clearly by evidence.
